rules.text: Use four principal parts. Present 1sg/pl use the present stem; present 2/3sg have the audited mutation/consonant changes. Past1/3sg normally share the singular stem; past2sg uses the plural stem plus -e, and all plural persons use -on. findan requires the separately printed exception.
Infinitive and past participle are citation/reference support only. No new perfect, passive, infinitive clause, participial agreement or prefix rule follows from a principal-parts table.
Class I normally ī : ā : i : i. Snīðan changes ð to d in plural-based past forms and participle. Contracted wrēon has a special present and h/g stems.
Class II normally ēo or ū : ēa : u : o. Present2/3sg ēo→īe and ū→ȳ; Cook also allows ī for īe. cēosan s/r, sēoðan ð/d, and tēon h/g are lexical changes.

III has several present/past-singular families, not one interchangeable vowel formula: bindan i/a/u/u, helpan e/ea/u/o, gieldan ie/ea/u/o, weorpan eo/ea/u/o, berstan e/æ/u/o. All those selected vowels are short. weorðan adds ð/d; winnan reduces nn; findan, bregdan and fēolan need explicit exception notes.

Dental d/t+ð gives tt (or t); d+st gives tst. s+st/ð gives st; ð before st may disappear and ð+ð may reduce. Geminates reduce before consonantal endings. g/h alternatives require the stated long-vowel/liquid environment; do not substitute h indiscriminately.

Cook permits full -est/-eð forms as well as syncopated cells. Their vowel can preserve an older mutated stem or be restored analogically; the audit selects complete contracted rows and records specifically checked variants rather than generating every possible full-ending spelling. A correct documented variant is not wrong merely for differing from the recall target.

Recognize present plural -e before an immediately following subject pronoun (Cook binde wē). This is conditioned by word order and is not a global alternative to -að after a preceding subject; production tasks may retain subject-before-verb.

Tōberstan and forweorðan are independently sourced lexemes, then expanded by identified base morphology. Their meanings and intransitive source frames are separate. No arbitrary prefix attachment or sense composition is licensed.
Extend prior preverbal ne to the introduced noncontracting strong indicatives. Keep negative copula, nillan and other contracted systems outside this extension.
Ordinary weorðan become can take a nominative predicate adjective agreeing with the subject. The finite indicative system does not promote old supplied passive constructions.

The finite paradigm does not establish object case. In particular helpan permits genitive or dative (selected dative here); bēodan command, gieldan repayment, bregdan instrumental use and other complements require separate teaching. Morphology-only verbs may be practised with person/tense labels without composing an unsupported clause.
